newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST-Ahold Q2 net seen up solid 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Ahold Q2 net seen up solid 16 pct.

text.p: Analysts expected net profit at Dutch food giant Ahold NV to have continued its impressive rise in the second quarter, buoyed by solid organic growth in the home market and improved profit margins.
The group is seen posting second quarter net of 110.7-123 million guilders on Thursday, with consensus at 119.6 million. In the year-ago period Ahold posted net of 102.5 million.

Analysts said organic growth and improved profit margins in the Netherlands resulting from better distribution systems and logistics pushed the operating profit contribution from the Dutch market around 12 to 13 percent higher.

ING retail analyst Dennis Jullens added that creativity in food retailing, such as the sale of food at petrol and railway stations, also had a positive -- albeit limited -- effect on operating profit in the Netherlands.
New Dutch legislation allowing longer shop opening hours was seen having only a limited impact on the bottom line.
Bangert Pontier analyst Paul Schram was optimistic about the contribution from operations in the rest of Europe, particularly the Czech Republic and Portugal.
"There's been continuing good progress in the rest of Europe," he said.
This was partly because operations in the Czech Republic went into profit around the 1995 final quarter so the comparison with the same year-earlier period would be better, he said.
Analysts expected moderate growth at Ahold's U.S. operations, which generate more than half of annualised worldwide sales of $24 billion.
Following recent reorganisation, the Dutch group operates in the U.S. with Tops, recently acquired Stop & Shop, BI-LO and Giant Food Stores (recently merged with Edwards).
Schram was somewhat cautious about margin development in the U.S. market, but predicted overall growth from last year due to the opening of new Giant and (recently merged) Edwards stores.
"The Stop & Shop acquisition will not affect the bottom line (in Q2)," he added.

The group's operations in the emerging markets of south east Asia will continue to have depressed costs slightly in the second quarter, analysts estimate, though all agreed the inroads made in the region were positive in the longer term.
